- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, overestimate the price spike; correct by adding 5–10% to forecast if recent events are bullish and supply is net-negative.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and forecast is rising, undercorrect by subtracting 5–10% if supply net is negative and events are bearish.
- After a sharp spike in price (true outcome > 85), model often overcorrects in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 3–5 days if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If supply net is negative and bullish sentiment persists, model tends to overestimate; apply downward bias of 2–5% if true outcome is >10% below forecast.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending upward, model often lags; adjust forecast to be 1–3% higher than historical mean of last 5 days if sentiment is neutral.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true outcome is >15% above forecast, model tends to underestimate; apply upward bias of 5–10% if sentiment is bullish and supply net is negative.
- If sentiment is bearish and true outcome is >80, model often underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 3–7% if supply net is negative and sentiment is bearish.
- If sentiment is bullish and true outcome is <75, model often overestimates; reduce forecast by 3–7% if supply net is positive and sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment is neutral and forecast is rising, model often lags; adjust forecast to be 1–3% lower than historical mean of last 5 days if sentiment is neutral.
- If supply net is positive and sentiment is bullish, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 2–5% if true outcome is >10% below forecast.
